newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares pause, then resume strong rally.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares pause, then resume strong rally.

text.p: Italian shares rapidly resumed their positive trend on Tuesday after some early weakness when subdued U.S inflation figures prompted a rise on Wall Street and buyers soon returned to Milan to drive stock prices higher.

"After a number of days of strong gains it was time to pause this morning, but the U.S. data eased rate rise fears in the U.S. and gave a good reason to jump back on the buying bandwagon," said one share dealer in Milan.
The all-share Milan stock market Mibtel index rose 3.46 percent to 12,080 while the blue chip Mib30 index increased 3.68 percent to 18,162.

U.S. December consumer price index inflation rose 0.3 percent, in line with forecasts, while core CPI increased 0.1 percent in comparison with 0.2 percent expected. U.S. retail sales in December rose 0.6 percent compared to a 0.5 percent rise forecast.
"It was the core rate that investors focused on and with the rapid rise in domestic bonds, shares were pulled up in the the general euphoria," said the Milan share dealer.

Most blue chips showed strong gains with ENI up 2.0 percent to 9,099 lire and Fiat rose 4.19 percent at 5,201 lire, while Olivetti lagged, only up 1.55 percent at 623.4 lire as talks continued on the sale of its personal computer company.

Telecom stocks were strong after 1996 results from Telecom Italia late Monday with the group's shares ending up 4.81 percent at 4,664 lire, while STET was 5.37 percent firmer at 7,498 lire, and TIM rose 3.36 percent to 4,342 lire.

Pirelli shares closed up 3.41 percent at 3,217 lire. The group announced just at the close of trading that it was buying up the shares and warrants that it did not already own in its majority-owned Pirelli Tyre Holding NV unit.
